selected_comments.body:
Magic number. My Codex side chat says:

> It encodes the assumption that contact starts at `0.5`, leaving an interval of length `0.5`.
> 
> The intended normalization is:
> 
```rs
progress = (phase - contact) / (1 - contact)
```
> 
> The scale should be derived from those endpoints, ideally inside a typed interval-normalization operation. That keeps the contact phase as the single source of truth.
It seems `type Output` should be `SpeedResult<SignedSpeed>`; a large negative speed plus a small nonnegative speed will be negative (i.e. signed, _not_ nonnegative).

In how many other locations would it be helpful to make an "open interval" type, consisting of a lower and upper, with the _guarantee_ that `upper > lower`? So that we may make this a method of that. (Not in scope of this PR.)

observations: Contact threshold is one typed UnitInterval::HALF constant.
Launch span275 is phase*2.0 before contact, so contact-only repair leaves duplicate HALF policy in directly connected producer.
Contact334–338 manually computes (phase-contact)*2 then checked smoothstep; both transition and lower-body recipients guard phase>=contact.

At contact the launch contribution reaches directional dive, while recovery begins at zero progress. Launch is linear and contact recovery cubic; do not accidentally smooth the upper-body launch when unifying normalization.
transition.phase is already admitted UnitInterval, then48 extracts primitive and redundantly clamps.
49–53 separately normalizes ZERO..contact and contact..ONE through raw terrain smoothstep; latter result is complemented to release pelvis. Both procedural sides are cubic.
54 re-admits raw amount into private DiveInfluence; its from_factor repeats finite/clamp/unit checks.

DiveInfluence is role-specific wrapper used by quaternion rotation/slerp; preserve meaningful role wrapper but provide infallible From<UnitInterval> for typed production path. Keep native fraction extraction only when multiplying angle and calling quaternion slerp.
Procedural system returns unit and currently warns/continues on typed failure; preserve explicit error handling rather than panic/default fallback.
Generic raw smoothstep derives ratio from arbitrary edges then clamps and evaluates cubic; it has no explicit equal/reversed bounds contract.
Replacing dive callers does not prove all other raw helper callers use equivalent ordered semantics. Broad terrain/IK migration is outside this bounded packet.
Private checked finite0..1 leaf with ZERO/ONE/HALF, complement, fallible cubic and closed multiplication already exists.
Existing FractionError distinguishes nonfinite and outside-unit values; new normalization needs distinct nonincreasing bounds error.
Current handwritten Display/Error can be derived with existing thiserror dependency when changing this owner; no old-message compatibility constraint.
Generic NonnegativeSpeed+SignedSpeed currently returns SpeedResult<NonnegativeSpeed>, excluding a mathematically valid negative sum.
SignedSpeed is finite-only and existing constructor admits negatives; no new speed type required.

Direct same-owner consumer checked_lerp67–70 promises NonnegativeSpeed. Its lerp weights/endpoints mathematically yield nonnegative result, but after signed Add result it must explicitly re-admit this guarantee at the speed owner.
Addition can overflow even with finite inputs, so signed result still requires SpeedResult and explicit Overflow mapping; do not return infallible SignedSpeed or saturate.
Do not use nonnegative_part to mask a negative arithmetic result in checked_lerp. It is an existing independent intentional forward-only clamp.

minimal_complete_recommendation.owner_operation: UnitInterval::clamped_inverse_lerp(self, lower:Self, upper:Self)->FractionResult<Self> on existing leaf. Check lower>=upper first and return FractionError::NonIncreasingBounds, even when value would otherwise clamp to endpoint. For valid interval return ZERO/ONE outside, otherwise admit (self.0-lower.0)/(upper.0-lower.0) via from_fraction within owner. Distinct finite ordered unit endpoints guarantee positive representable span; no explicit raw scale2 or new ratio owner needed.
callers: evaluation launch: phase.clamped_inverse_lerp(UnitInterval::ZERO,DIVE_GROUND_CONTACT_PHASE)?; keep linear launch progress.
evaluation contact: phase.clamped_inverse_lerp(DIVE_GROUND_CONTACT_PHASE,UnitInterval::ONE)?.smoothstep()?; typed comparisons can replace primitive branch thresholds.

client procedural: typed phase<=contact; launch interval ZERO..contact then smoothstep; release interval contact..ONE then smoothstep and complement. Widen that UnitInterval into DiveInfluence without extracting/rechecking scalar. Retain native scalar extraction only angle/quaternion boundary.
minimal_complete_recommendation.error_receivers: Extend existing From<FractionError> for AnimationValueError with NonIncreasingBounds carrying UnitInterval quantity. Existing animation result and client warn/continue handling remain coherent. No equal/reversed-step fallback or compatibility behavior needed.
minimal_complete_recommendation.addition: Change impl Add<SignedSpeed> for NonnegativeSpeed Output to SpeedResult<SignedSpeed>. Use signed admission for sum with nonfinite mapped to Overflow. checked_lerp consumes signed sum and explicitly re-admits nonnegative arithmetic inside same existing owner; use existing private field access there instead of a new application primitive adapter. TryFrom<SignedSpeed> for NonnegativeSpeed is only necessary if another actual typed consumer needs it.
